concepts.def: Information about where food was grown, reared or caught and how it was produced, which informs consumers about its origin.
The distance food travels from where it is produced to where it is eaten, often used as an indicator of its environmental impact.
Eating foods at the time of year they are naturally harvested locally, which can cut cost and environmental impact and improve flavour.
Food produced without most artificial pesticides and fertilisers and with higher animal-welfare standards, certified to defined organic rules.
A certification ensuring producers in developing countries receive a fair, guaranteed price and better working conditions for their goods.
Having reliable access to enough safe, affordable and nutritious food, a concern affected by climate, trade and population growth.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Food Provenance and Food Choice — a core area of GCSE Food Preparation and Nutrition.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Food Provenance and Food Choice brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Food Provenance and Food Choice.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Buying strawberries grown locally in summer rather than imported in winter follows the principle of:
options: Seasonality
Pasteurisation
Fortification
Gelatinisation

mcqs.q: The Fairtrade mark mainly guarantees that producers receive:
options: A fair, guaranteed price
Free packaging
Tax-free goods
Faster delivery

mcqs.q: Information about where and how a food was produced is known as its:
options: Provenance
Provenance tax
Allergen list
Portion size

mcqs.q: Do fewer 'food miles' always mean a smaller environmental impact?
options: Food miles measure the calories in food.
Usually lower, but not always, since production methods and transport type also affect impact.
Eating different foods on different days of the week.
Food miles are the only thing that determines environmental impact.

mcqs.q: Does the Fairtrade mark guarantee the food is organic?
options: Fairtrade means the food is free.
Fairtrade and organic mean the same thing.
Eating different foods on different days of the week.
No; Fairtrade is about fair prices and conditions for producers, not organic production.

mcqs.q: What does 'seasonality' mean when choosing food?
options: Buying any food that is currently on special offer.
Eating different foods on different days of the week.
Fairtrade means the food is free.
Eating foods when they are naturally harvested locally.
